newsitem.title: USA: General Mills Q2 mkt share, EPS seen up - analysts.
newsitem.headline: General Mills Q2 mkt share, EPS seen up - analysts.

text.p: General Mills Inc nabbed an increased share of the U.S. ready-to-eat cereal market in its fiscal second quarter, which is expected to contribute to slightly higher quarterly earnings, analysts said.

BT Securities analyst John O'Neil said he estimated that General Mills' market share for the second quarter ended in November will be up one to two percentage points from its share of 23.5 percent in the year ago period.
Despite promotional costs to launch new cereals, which contributed to the market share gain, General Mills is expected to report a 3.3 percent rise in quarterly earnings.
Overall, General Mills' domestic cereal sales volume is expected to rise five to six percent in the second quarter, Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez sid.
"However, some of this volume is being propelled by promotions," she added. "The bottom line will not fully benefit from that."
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates for the second quarter is $0.95 a share, which would be up about 3.3 percent from $0.92 a year ago.
During the quarter, General Mills introduced three new cereals -- Betty Crocker Dutch Apple and Cinnamon Streusel and its new French Toast Crunch.

But General Mills may not be able to hold onto all the gains in market share from the new cereals. New products typically show a jump in purchases in the near-term and level off later on, analysts said.
